help.intro: A short text of about 120 words with real facts about Hamburg, told in numbers: how many people live there, how many bridges the city has (more than Venice and Amsterdam together), how old the harbour is and what the river is called. All numbers are real and were checked. You need only what you have learnt: numbers up to a million written as words, Hamburg hat / Hamburg ist, and the question words Wie viele? (how many), Wie alt? (how old), Wo? (where). Read the text once for the gist, then take each question and find the number it asks for.
help.tips[0].title: Big numbers in words
help.tips[0].text: Hundred = hundert, thousand = tausend, million = eine Million (plural: zwei Millionen). German writes a number as one long word up to a million: zweitausendfünfhundert (2,500). Years are read in hundreds: 1189 = elfhundertneunundachtzig. Watch the order in two-digit numbers: 89 = neunundachtzig, nine-and-eighty.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Hamburg has almost two million inhabitants.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The city has about two thousand five hundred bridges.
help.tips[0].check.why: neun-und-achtzig = nine and eighty = 89. German says the ones before the tens.
help.tips[1].text: Wie viele Brücken hat Hamburg? asks for a number of things. Wie alt ist der Hafen? asks for an age. Wo liegt Hamburg? asks for a place and gets an answer with in or an: in Norddeutschland, an der Elbe. Find the question word first, then hunt for that kind of answer in the text.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Where is Hamburg? Hamburg lies in the north of Germany, on the Elbe.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: How old is the harbour? The harbour is over eight hundred years old.
help.tips[1].check.q: Which question asks for a place?
help.tips[1].check.why: Wo = where. Wie viele asks for a number, wie alt for an age.
help.remember[0]: hundert, tausend, eine Million / zwei Millionen; ones before tens: neunundachtzig = 89.
help.remember[1]: Wo? = place (in, an), Wie viele? = how many, Wie alt? = how old.
help.exam: Short factual texts with numbers and multiple-choice questions are a typical reading task at this level, and exactly what a city guide or a poster looks like.
help.hook: Almost two million people, two and a half thousand bridges, a harbour older than eight hundred years. Read Hamburg in numbers.
help.vocab[4].example: Jedes Jahr kommen etwa achttausend Schiffe.
passageTranslation:
Hamburg is a city in the north of Germany. The city lies on the Elbe. The Elbe is a river. It is over a thousand kilometres long and comes from the Czech Republic.

Almost two million people live in Hamburg. Hamburg is the second-largest city in Germany. Only Berlin is bigger.

Hamburg has a lot of water: the Elbe, the Alster and many canals. That is why the city also has very many bridges: about two thousand five hundred! That is more bridges than in Venice and Amsterdam together.

The harbour is the heart of Hamburg. It is very old: the harbour has its birthday on 7 May 1189. So it is over eight hundred years old. Today the port of Hamburg is the biggest port in Germany. Every year about eight thousand ships come.

Hamburg also has a famous concert hall: the Elbphilharmonie. It is 110 metres high and stands right by the water. From the top you see the harbour, the Elbe and the whole city.

questions[1].explanation: "In Hamburg wohnen fast zwei Millionen Menschen." 2,500 is the number of bridges, 8,000 the ships.
questions[1].questionTranslation: How many people live in Hamburg?
questions[2].explanation: "Hamburg ist die zweitgrößte Stadt in Deutschland. Nur Berlin ist größer."
questions[2].questionTranslation: Which city in Germany is bigger than Hamburg?
questions[3].explanation: "Hamburg hat sehr viel Wasser: die Elbe, die Alster und viele Kanäle. Darum hat die Stadt auch sehr viele Brücken." Darum = that is why.
questions[3].questionTranslation: Why does Hamburg have so many bridges?
questions[3].optionsTranslation[0]: because the city is very old
questions[3].optionsTranslation[1]: because the city has a lot of water: rivers and canals
questions[3].optionsTranslation[2]: because Hamburg is bigger than Berlin
questions[3].optionsTranslation[3]: because very many ships come into the harbour every year
questions[4].explanation: "etwa zweitausendfünfhundert" = about 2,500. Listen for tausend in the middle of the word.
questions[4].questionTranslation: About how many bridges does Hamburg have?
questions[5].explanation: "Der Hafen hat Geburtstag am 7. Mai 1189." That is why it is over 800 years old.
questions[6].explanation: "Hamburg hat auch ein berühmtes Konzerthaus: die Elbphilharmonie."
questions[6].optionsTranslation[2]: a concert hall by the water
